summary.text: 八 is the numeral “eight,” already used as a number in oracle-bone inscriptions. Its two strokes have traditionally been read as suggesting separation, but that proposed original meaning and its relation to “eight” remain uncertain.

formation.text: 八 is an indivisible graph. The traditional account reads its diverging strokes as separation; other proposals connect it with 分 or 別, or interpret it as a concrete gesture or object. Early numeral uses do not show that separation came first, and the original referent is unresolved.

components.text: The whole graph consists of two diverging strokes. In the traditional interpretation they suggest separation, but no particular object or gesture is established. 八 is not a compound of modern components.

history.text: Catalogs record oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript and seal-script forms. The curated oracle-bone and Warring States bronze examples show diverging strokes, but do not establish a sequence of graphic change or determine the graph’s origin.

uncertainties.text: The traditional separation interpretation competes with proposals that 八 was an early graph for 分, represented 別, or depicted a concrete gesture or object. The original referent and the relative standing of these accounts remain unresolved.

Oracle-bone inscriptions already use 八 as a numeral, but the cited examples have no independently verified absolute dates here, and no earlier written use meaning “separate” is provided. The evidence does not establish that separation preceded “eight.”

senses.text: Oracle-bone examples use 八 as a cardinal numeral, including in expressions for eight animals and in a month expression. These attest early numeral use, not a hypothetical original meaning.
Oracle-bone month usage and later examples show 八 in month and year expressions with ordinal value. The evidence does not date a distinct development from the cardinal sense.
八 is also glossed “all around” or “all sides.” No dated history connects this use to the numeral “eight.”

A traditional interpretation reads the diverging strokes as separation. No early written example of 八 with this meaning is provided, so it remains a proposed original sense rather than an established earliest attestation.

developments.text: One proposal is that a graph associated with “separate” was reused to write the numeral word “eight” because the words sounded alike or similarly. No earlier written use for separation or historical sound comparison for the proposed source word is established, so the borrowing account and sequence remain uncertain.

limitations.text: The original referent, any earlier written use for separation, and the sound of the proposed source word for the borrowing account remain unresolved. The supplied reconstruction is for the numeral word 八, not that proposed source word.
The “all around; all sides” gloss has no dated semantic history connecting it to “eight.”

overview.text: 八 is the numeral “eight,” already used as a number in oracle-bone inscriptions. The traditional idea that it first meant “separate” is uncertain.

components.text: The whole graph is traditionally read as two strokes turning apart to suggest separation; no specific object is identified.

takeaway.text: The proposed reuse for “eight” depends on a sound similarity with an alleged separation word, but neither that match nor an earlier written use is established.
